key_insight: A quantum co-design workflow can simulate inhomogeneous many-body neutrino fast flavor evolution while linking ideal accuracy, NISQ execution, and fault-tolerant resource estimates in one model.
engineering_relevance: The paper shows that a restricted interaction graph enables practical circuit-depth and T-gate budgeting up to 50 particles, making resource planning for quantum neutrino simulations more actionable.
method: Mapped an inhomogeneous neutrino Hamiltonian with advection and finite-range interactions to TEBD2 product-formula circuits.
Built QCNO to compare exact many-body evolution, backend-aware noisy execution, and fault-tolerant resource estimation.
Analyzed entanglement, magic, circuit depth, and T-gate costs under open and closed boundary conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exact many-body reproduction through N=30, noisy-backend polarization RMSEs around 0.1–0.3, and an ideal TEBD2 error near 10^-3 that drives a synthesis tolerance of about 10^-7.
watch_item: The noisy-backend results still have sizable polarization error, so near-term hardware performance may remain limited without better error mitigation or circuit synthesis.
paper_title: Quantum Co-Design of Inhomogeneous Many-Body Neutrino Fast Flavor Transformation
